transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. I'm Santiago. I guess I'm here because of some trouble I've been having with eating. 

What really worries me is that once I start picking at food late at night, I just... I can't seem to stop. I'll actually tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago,' but my hand just keeps going back for more. It honestly feels like I don't get to make the decision anymore once I start.

After these late-night eating episodes, do you do anything to try to compensate or make up for what you've eaten—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or restricting food the next day?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't... I would never make myself throw up, and I don't take pills or anything like that. 

I mean, I usually feel pretty guilty about it the next morning, but I don't try to starve myself to make up for it, and I'm definitely not going to the gym to run for hours. I just get up, go to work at the warehouse, and eat my regular meals during the day.
Besides the eating at night, do you find yourself pulling out your hair, picking at your skin, or doing any other repetitive behaviors that you feel you can't control?

No, I don't do anything like that. I don't pull my hair or... pick at my skin or anything. It's really just the eating at night that I feel like I lose control over. I don't have any other habits like what you're describing.

When you're eating late at night and feel like you can't stop, how much food would you say you're typically consuming? Are we talking about enormous quantities that would be unusual for most people, or more like regular portions that just feel out of control?

Well, it's definitely a lot. I mean... it's not just an extra plate. 

On some nights after work, I can go through several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, a bunch of tortillas, and honestly whatever rice or beans are left over from dinner. And I do it all while just standing there in the kitchen, almost like I'm just cleaning up the leftovers, you know? But when you look at it all together... yeah, it's a pretty large amount of food. It's definitely more than what most people would eat in one sitting.
How often would you say these late-night eating episodes happen? Is it happening every night, a few times a week, or less frequently than that?

Well, for the past several months, it's been happening... I'd say most weeks at least once. It's usually on a night when my wife made a big dinner so there are plenty of leftovers, and everyone else has already gone to bed. So, yeah, at least once a week.

When you think about these late-night eating episodes, how much does it bother you or affect your life? Does it cause you significant distress or interfere with work, relationships, or how you feel about yourself?

It bothers me, yeah. I mean, it hasn't messed up my work or anything. I'm still getting to my shipping and receiving shifts and handling my responsibilities there just fine. 

But... it does affect things at home a bit. I've actually started avoiding some of the late family time we usually spend hanging out in the kitchen. I just... I'm worried someone will notice how uneasy I am around the food. So I just kind of stay away to avoid it. It's definitely getting to me in that way.

When you're standing in the kitchen at night before you start eating, do you feel like you have a choice about whether to eat, or does the urge to eat feel so strong that you know you're going to lose control no matter what?

Well, that's what really worries me. Before I start, I might think I'm just going to have one little bite. But once I start picking at the food... I'll literally tell myself, "That's enough, Santiago," but my hand just keeps going back for more. It's like I don't even get to make the decision anymore. I just can't stop it once it starts.
